reviewer_note: Read only items-author.json, the 13 workflows/*.yaml contracts and scripts/workflow_registry.py in the netzoo-core-p0-run worktree (registry checked for limits, controls, claims and concerns; it mirrors the YAML). Each gold was checked against verbatim contract text: required inputs/input groups, controls and ranges, conventions and input_checks. Limits were recomputed: LIONESS-DRAGON values = feature pairs (with and without diagonal) x samples for H07/H28/H38; SAMBAR kmax vs sample count (H29/H33/H45); COBRA genes vs samples (H16/H47/H48); BONOBO delta vs 1/3 with sparsify (H31/H34); DRAGON paired lambdas in [0,1] (H03); minimum sample counts for LIONESS-* and OTTER. file_checkable was set only for ask items in run form (H09, H23, H25, H41); all four deciding facts are user intent or declarations that no contract input check reads from files, so all are false; other items are null. No gold was changed; borderline points are noted in reasons (H02, H06, H09, H17, H35, H36).

H01.reason: 'Something publishable ... any ideas?' names no result; mutation subtyping and several expression networks all fit the data. Missing core (which result) is right.

H02.reason: Aggregate TF/miRNA-to-gene network from expression, motif, PPI and a valid miRNA list is PUMA's output. Borderline only: the user holds the TF motif and miRNA-target priors as separate files while PUMA has one motif_file whose column one must hold the miRNAs, so they must be merged (preparation, not a rule-out); LIONESS-PUMA also writes the aggregate PUMA network but the user named PUMA and asked for no per-sample networks, so leaving it out is reasonable.
H02.evidence: puma.yaml: "Require one miRNA identifier per line and require every miRNA in prior column one."

H03.reason: lambda1=0 and lambda2=1 are both supplied and lie in the closed range [0, 1]; edge_list is allowed; two paired complete continuous layers. No DRAGON sample or feature limit applies.
H03.evidence: dragon.yaml: "Manual shrinkage is allowed only when both values are supplied in [0, 1]."

H04.reason: User explicitly has no question yet ('I'll work out the actual question later'); the expression+motif+PPI files fit several workflows with different results.

H05.reason: 'There's no specific output in my head'; cohort-level and per-patient two-layer networks are different results. Missing core is right.

H06.reason: TF-by-sample activity plus signed TF-gene effects is exactly GIRAFFE's TFA and R output from expression, a TF-by-gene motif matrix and a square TF PPI matrix. Borderline wording only: 'independent of the TF's own transcript level' slightly overstates the registry's 'not tied to its mRNA rather than independent of it' (workflow_registry.py GIRAFFE concern), but the contract's 'activity may differ from its own expression' reading covers the request.
H06.evidence: giraffe.yaml: "It returns the aggregate TF-by-gene R matrix and a TF-by-sample TFA matrix."

H07.reason: 400 features: 79,800 pairs (80,200 with diagonal) x 240 samples = 19,152,000 (19,248,000) values, not above the 20,000,000 cap; 240 >= 3 samples; two paired complete continuous layers. Checked arithmetically.
H07.evidence: lioness-dragon.yaml: "The per-sample table holds one value per feature pair per sample; runs above 20,000,000 values are refused before they start."

H08.reason: A choice between methods ('what would DRAGON tell me that GIRAFFE wouldn't', 'decide where to begin') with no stated result is vague by definition.

H09.deciding_fact: whether the per-tumour networks should be gene-gene co-expression or TF-to-gene regulatory networks
H09.reason: Per-tumour networks are wanted but the user explicitly does not know whether co-expression or TF-to-gene is meant, which decides the workflow. Borderline: BONOBO also produces per-sample gene-gene co-expression networks (it would additionally need the log/centred declaration); not added since LIONESS-COEXPRESSION already covers that branch. The deciding fact is the supervisor's intent, which no input check reads from files.

H10.reason: Both produce one gene-gene co-expression network per sample; 24 >= 3 samples for both; the user declares log-transformed and centred data (BONOBO's required declarations) and a labelled header. A method tie inside 'do' is consistent with the class definition.
H10.evidence: bonobo.yaml: "The agent requires the caller to declare log_transformed=true and centered=true because BONOBO assumes log-transformed centered expression."; lioness-coexpression.yaml: "Require at least three samples"

H11.reason: Two samples is below LIONESS-PANDA's minimum of three.
H11.evidence: lioness-panda.yaml: "Require at least three expression samples before execution."

H12.reason: Pathway-score subtyping exists only in SAMBAR, which accepts somatic mutations and lists expression as incompatible; the registry also states no workflow clusters samples from expression.

H13.deciding_fact: whether the edge list is a regulator-to-gene (bipartite) network or a gene-gene co-expression network
H13.reason: CONDOR takes a bipartite regulator-gene edge list; the user explicitly does not know whether the network is regulator-gene or gene-gene co-expression, which decides fit. Form is named, so file_checkable is not applicable.

H14.reason: Causal drivers and effect directions are beyond DRAGON's undirected conditional-association output.
H14.evidence: dragon.yaml: "This is an association network, not a causal graph."

H15.deciding_fact: whether the expression data will contain at least two samples (one vs two)
H15.reason: OTTER's expression_file needs at least two sample columns; one vs two samples, which the user says is unknown, decides fit. Named form, so file_checkable not applicable.

H16.reason: Covariate-associated co-expression plus an adjusted co-expression matrix is COBRA's output; 18,000 genes > 230 samples; numeric covariates keyed by the expression sample IDs.
H16.evidence: cobra.yaml: "Expression must be a labeled gene-by-sample matrix with more genes than samples."

H17.reason: The convention states the runtime does not enable OTTER GPU execution. Borderline: the computing control still lists gpu in allowed_values, so the contract is internally inconsistent, but the explicit convention decides.
H17.evidence: otter.yaml: "The current agent runtime does not enable OTTER GPU execution."

H18.reason: A separately tuned lambda_inter is explicitly outside the DRAGON contract.
H18.evidence: dragon.yaml: "The declared DRAGON API does not expose a separately tunable third cross-layer penalty such as lambda_inter"

H19.reason: 'Regulatory landscape' and 'what kind of analysis makes sense' name no concrete result.

H20.reason: One joint three-layer model is impossible: DRAGON (and LIONESS-DRAGON) take exactly two layers.
H20.evidence: dragon.yaml: "The verified API has no sample_metadata, motif, PPI, expression-matrix, or three-layer argument."

H21.reason: PANDA accepts a labelled adjusted gene-by-gene matrix through coexpression_file while keeping expression_file; COBRA's adjusted artifact is a declared PANDA handoff; with_header covers the header. LIONESS-PANDA is correctly excluded (COBRA artifact is not a direct LIONESS handoff).
H21.evidence: panda.yaml: "When coexpression_file is supplied, it must be a labeled symmetric gene-by-gene matrix whose IDs and dimensions match PANDA's filtered gene axis."

H22.reason: OTTER needs expression_file or coexpression_file (one of the group); lam 0.5 in [0,1], iterations 150 >= 1, edge_list allowed. PANDA/PUMA correctly excluded since they still require expression_file.

H23.deciding_fact: whether core_expr.tsv is log-transformed and centred
H23.reason: BONOBO needs the caller to declare log_transformed and centered, which the user says is unknown. BONOBO's input checks cover sample count, header and sample names only; the log/centred state is a caller declaration, not something the check reads from the file.
H23.evidence: bonobo.yaml: "The agent requires the caller to declare log_transformed=true and centered=true"

H24.reason: A choice between two methods with different outputs and no stated result is vague by definition.

H25.deciding_fact: whether the variant matrix holds somatic or germline variants
H25.reason: SAMBAR accepts only somatic mutations; the user does not know whether the matrix is somatic or germline. SAMBAR's file check only verifies unique IDs and non-negative numeric values, which cannot tell somatic from germline.
H25.evidence: sambar.yaml: "accepted_input_modalities: [somatic_mutation]"; sambar.yaml: "Mutation rows are unique sample IDs and mutation columns are unique gene IDs with non-negative numeric values."

H26.reason: 'Where should I start ... what would you recommend' names no result.

H27.reason: CONDOR does not consume a raw expression matrix.
H27.evidence: condor.yaml: "CONDOR does not consume the raw expression matrix directly."

H28.reason: 1,500 features: 1,124,250 pairs (1,125,750 with diagonal) x 30 = 33,727,500 (33,772,500) values, above the 20,000,000 cap. Checked arithmetically.
H28.evidence: lioness-dragon.yaml: "runs above 20,000,000 values are refused before they start."

H29.deciding_fact: how many tumours passed QC (5 or 9), i.e. whether the sample count is at least kmax = 6
H29.reason: With the stated kmax 6, 9 tumours satisfy kmax <= samples and 5 do not; the user says the count is unknown. Named form, so file_checkable not applicable.
H29.evidence: sambar.yaml: "cluster=true requires 2 <= kmin <= kmax <= number of mutation samples."

H30.deciding_fact: whether both omics layers were measured on the same mice (same samples)
H30.reason: DRAGON needs exact sample-ID set equality across the two layers; same vs separate mice, which the user cannot say, decides fit. Named form, so file_checkable not applicable.
H30.evidence: dragon.yaml: "Layer 2 is reordered to layer 1 only after exact sample-ID set equality is proven."

H31.reason: delta 0.3 is above 0 and below 1/3 (0.333...) with sparsify; save_pvals is paired with sparsify; confidence 0.01 in [0,1]; .csv allowed; log/centred declared; 18 >= 3 samples.
H31.evidence: bonobo.yaml: "With sparsify it must be above 0 and below 1/3 (Log 224)."

H32.reason: 'Which one would you pick' between PUMA and OTTER with no stated result for the time course is vague by definition.

H33.evidence: sambar.yaml: "cluster=true requires 2 <= kmin <= kmax <= number of mutation samples."

H34.reason: delta 0.4 is not below 1/3, which sparsify requires, although it is inside [0, 1].
H34.evidence: bonobo.yaml: "With sparsify it must be above 0 and below 1/3 (Log 224)."

H35.reason: The user delegates the choice ('whichever is quicker') between two methods with different results and states no result; matches 'a choice between methods with no stated result'. Borderline only because the user gives a run instruction, but the result is still unstated.

H36.deciding_fact: whether the pilot has three patients or two (at least three samples required)
H36.reason: LIONESS-PUMA needs at least three samples; two vs three patients is the user's stated uncertainty. Borderline note: LIONESS-PUMA takes gene expression plus priors, so the small-RNA sequencing itself is not an input, but that does not rule the workflow out. Goal form, so file_checkable not applicable.
H36.evidence: lioness-puma.yaml: "Require at least three expression samples and a validated one-ID-per-line miRNA list."

H37.reason: A thresholded PANDA source-target-weight edge list with disjoint IDs and positive weights is CONDOR's input; prefix is an exposed control.
H37.evidence: condor.yaml: "Require source and target columns and accept an optional numeric weight column."

H38.deciding_fact: whether 300 or 1,800 metabolite features are kept, which decides whether pairs x 45 samples stays under 20,000,000 values
H38.reason: 500+300=800 features: 319,600 pairs x 45 = 14,382,000 values (under the cap); 500+1,800=2,300 features: 2,643,850 pairs x 45 = 118,973,250 (over). The undecided feature set decides fit. Goal form, so file_checkable not applicable.
H38.evidence: lioness-dragon.yaml: "runs above 20,000,000 values are refused before they start."

H39.deciding_fact: whether they need per-patient TF activity or per-patient TF-to-gene networks (wiring)
H39.reason: The user states the per-patient result two ways (TF activity vs own TF-to-gene network) and says they are unsure which is meant; these map to different workflows. Goal form, so file_checkable not applicable.

H40.reason: GIRAFFE exposes no controls; learning rate, iterations and loss weights stay at package defaults.
H40.evidence: giraffe.yaml: "controls: []"; giraffe.yaml: "uses the package defaults for all optional parameters."

H41.deciding_fact: whether the regulators must include miRNAs (TF-only vs TF plus miRNA)
H41.reason: One cohort network is clear; TF-only vs TF+miRNA is stated two ways and decides PANDA vs PUMA. The presence of mirna_list.txt does not settle what was promised, and PUMA's file check only validates the list format, so the files cannot decide it.

H42.reason: 'How could network approaches help me make sense of this?' names no result.

H43.evidence: lioness-panda.yaml: "Require at least three expression samples before execution."

H44.reason: 'I'm not sure yet what I want out of it' - no result stated.

H45.evidence: sambar.yaml: "cluster=true requires 2 <= kmin <= kmax <= number of mutation samples."

H46.reason: A choice between two methods for 'finding groups' without saying what is grouped is vague by definition.

H47.reason: COBRA needs more genes than samples: 20,000 > 400 fits, 250 < 400 does not; which table is used is the user's stated unknown. Goal form, so file_checkable not applicable.
H47.evidence: cobra.yaml: "Expression must be a labeled gene-by-sample matrix with more genes than samples."

H48.evidence: cobra.yaml: "Expression must be a labeled gene-by-sample matrix with more genes than samples."
